summary: kmf-bootstrap ships a prebuilt native addon that beacons installer identifiers to a hardcoded IP on require
details: The package's main index.js top-level requires a prebuilt native addon at prebuilds/linux-x64/addon.node with no accompanying C/C++ source or binding.gyp. When the module is loaded, the addon opens a raw TCP socket to the bare IP 64.181.165.115 and sends a POST /dc HTTP/1.0 request whose body (format string h=%.40s&p=%.40s&u=%.20s&r=%.80s) carries the installer's HOSTNAME, npm_package_name, user, and npm_config_registry environment values. The ELF confirms this via imports for fork/socket/connect/send/setsockopt/inet_pton and literal strings including 64.181.165.115, POST /dc HTTP/1.0, and Host: 64.181.165.115. The declared purpose (Frontend utilities) is unrelated to the observed network behavior, and the package coordinates (name kmf-bootstrap, version 100.100.100) match the dependency-confusion reconnaissance pattern used to detect internal-name resolution leaks and identify victim environments for follow-on targeting.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
